title: How is MDX compiled, and which components may a stage document execute?
statement: Stage documents under `planning-content/stages/` are agent-authored content. MDX compiles to executable JavaScript, so the compilation strategy must state which components a document may reference and what happens to a reference outside that set.
notes: ⚠️ The load-bearing property is that agent-authored content must NOT implicitly become arbitrary application code. This project's whole discipline is that content is data the tool reads (#88 forbids authoring artifacts by hand precisely so the writer is a typed operation) — a document format whose default is 'anything in scope is callable' inverts that. The answer needs three parts: where compilation happens, the allowlist of components a document may use, and the behaviour on an unknown reference (refuse, or render inert). Refusing is consistent with how `checkJob` treats a shell-string command: refused rather than sanitised, because sanitising means guessing what the author meant.
